notes: F3 solver model: drainage allowance frozen at 30 mm/h [P] on not frozen: proposed 2026-11-25, awaiting Yuri's decision on FH8 (F3 report); 14 of 14 named runs finished. Calibrated on the city's two current-sea-level maps (limited 1.77 in/h, moderate 2.13 in/h); the 3.66 in/h run is a check against a 2080 map. Every number comes from the run folders, the city maps and the cache files listed as inputs. Captions: calibration_curve.png: Modelled area per city class (4 in to 1 ft, 1 ft and over) on the compared cells against the drainage allowance, one marker per calibration run, with the city map's area as a dashed line; below, the critical success index for wet (4 in or more) with model patches under a quarter acre removed (filtered) and without (raw), and for the deep class; green: the frozen value. Limit: 12 runs, each 1 h of uniform rain on the whole square; the city's maps come from another model, so a match is agreement with that model, not with observed flooding. hit_miss.png: Hit, miss and false alarm per compared cell at the proposed allowance, wet meaning 4 in or more, model patches under a quarter acre removed; grey: compared and dry in both; white: not compared (outside the study area, under a building footprint, a filled pit or water). Limit: a cell takes the city's class at its centre; a shift of one cell between the two maps counts as both a miss and a false alarm. water_balance.png: Rain, drained (the allowance), stored (change in water volume) and out (net outflow through the four edge cross-sections) per run, thousand m³, over the cells inside the boundary cells; the residual share of the rain is printed above. Limit: the fluxes are the solver's own outputs, so the balance tests their consistency, not that the rain or the drainage are right. atlas14.png: NOAA Atlas 14 60-minute depth at the study-area centre against return period, partial duration and annual maximum series, with their 90% bounds, and the three map intensities held for one hour. Limit: a point estimate for a 4 km area; the city's storm shape and duration are not a 60-minute block, so a placement is a reading, not the return period of the map.
